newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes again at 892.30 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes again at 892.30 - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) stepped into the interbank foreign exchange market for the second time on Friday, buying dollars at 892.30 won in the afternoon, dealers said.
After the intervention, the dollar rose to 893.10 won, they said.
The BOK bought dollars at 891.20 won before the morning close, dealers said.
The BOK never directly confirms its intevention.

Dealers said the central bank was seen intervening as the weakening dollar against the yen prompted the won's rise. They said the intervention showed the central bank's strong intention to keep the dollar/won rate over the 890 level.
Before the intervention, BOK assistant governor Shim Hoon said the dollar would stay above the current 890 won level, if the dollar/yen rate did not fall further.
The dollar slid below 123 yen, the first time it had dropped below that level since April 4.
"Unless the dollar/yen rate drops further from the current level, there is no reason for the dollar to fall below the 890 won mark," he said.
After the won opened at 892.10, it moved in a 893.40-890.80 range.
